title: feat: polish batch — letters sweep, cache keys, contrast, ai-status, italian tells, autopilot dates
body:
Owner-approved combined batch: six polish items plus the autopilot posting-date feature, one reviewable diff (42 files). Every item ran its own author → domain-critic → delta-verify chain; ~20 findings closed red-first along the way.

## Letters (export)

- **All six letter layouts stop hyphenating.** The four older layouts (Classic/Refined/Banded/Navy) justified without `hyphenate: false`, emitting U+00AD soft hyphens straight into the extracted text layer — the defect class #988 fixed for Sidebar/Monogram. The roster guard now covers the whole family, and a new test routes *every* layout through the choke point (extending the roster alone was a proven no-op — nothing exercised the old layouts). Justify stays on for all markets (full-measure columns; rivers are a non-issue). One preview SVG reflowed.
- **Nameless letters stop printing a date or salutation as the letterhead name.** `is_letterhead_name` (salutation/sign-off/subject/date) is ONE shared rule across PDF and both DOCX arms. Review caught the first version nesting the contact line under the new gate — a nameless letter with an attached contact profile lost both the date *and* the user's contact info in DOCX; contact now renders independently, mirroring the PDF, with `contact: Some(..)` as a mandated fixture axis (two prior tests hardcoding `None` is exactly how it shipped unverified). Bonus: salutation-opening letters had *never* emitted contact in DOCX — now they do. Suppression also exposed and fixed two latent Sidebar defects (a Typst `none.split` panic and an empty tinted rail).

## Small fixes

- **Company-brief cache key** now derives from `StageIdentity` wholesale (the canonical Completer→key-terms type, cross-referenced both ways) plus a new `Completer::search_backend()` term — review proved the resolved Native↔Exa backend flips on *credential presence at call time* and served the other vendor's brief for 7 days. Role is deliberately not a term (one paid search per company; documented as the cost tradeoff, not an omission).
- **Light-theme contrast, fixed centrally**: `text-foreground/15,/55,/60` + the entirely-uncovered `border-foreground/10–/25` family (73 call sites at `/10` alone, ~1.2:1 raw) join the remap. Folding `/60` in was forced by review math: mapped `/55` had overshot raw `/60`, inverting the token ordering — and raw `/60` was itself sub-AA despite a comment claiming otherwise. An ordering guard now pins `mapped(/55) < mapped(/60)`.
- **The dashboard AI-status widget stops lying in both directions.** Root cause: `system_health` probes only local Ollama, whatever provider is active — so cloud/CLI users saw a false "not available". The widget now uses the shared `useCanUseAI()` gate — whose `local-server` branch review then caught *never checking daemon liveness* (documented as "detected via a health probe"; no probe happened). The gate now requires `health.ai.ready` for Ollama with a distinct "Start Ollama" reason, healing all 14 call sites, and ships the repo's first unmocked test of the hook (every existing consumer test mocks it).
- **Italian AI-tell support**: a genuinely curated lexicon (13 lexical + 4 prose entries) through the four-rule checkability bar, frozen into the validators via the single-source `gen:prompts` path — Italian output already routed to the validators and simply fell into the uncurated empty arm. Review attacked every entry with truthful Italian sentences: `spirito di squadra` (a coach's real deliverable in object position) and `all'avanguardia` (the Futurist art movement) were demoted to prompt-only, each with a negative-control fixture in the entry's own surface form, mutation-checked by re-adding the entry. Elision makes apostrophe folding load-bearing in Italian (`l'esperienza`); proven by dual-spelling fixtures.

## Autopilot posting dates + per-card sorting

- **The posting date was parsed by every job board and dropped at one line** — `build_found_job` never copied it. It now threads through `FoundJob` (serde-defaulted; legacy stores load unchanged) with review-forced pins at both collapse points: `merge_found_jobs` (a mutation replacing the preserve-guard with an unconditional overwrite passed all 4115 tests until the new test) and `dedup_cross_source` (an Adzuna hit's date survived deduping against a dateless direct-board hit — previously lost permanently).
- **Each autopilot card sorts its own found-jobs list** (relevance default / newest / oldest), independently per card — the acceptance test renders two cards sorted differently at once. Sorting is a renderer-side view over a copy: the persisted order feeds AI-note recipient selection (ADR-020) and a dedicated non-mutation test pins that. Dated rows band before undated ones in *both* directions (a `?? 0` fallback regression is invisible in the descending sort — both are tested). Date chips reuse the Jobs page's relative-time helper; en+de keys.

## Also in this diff

`docs/NEXT_ISSUES.md` (the old deferred-items ledger, in-repo since July) is retired per owner decision — deleted, gitignored, every citation across docs/CSS/Rust comments reworded to stand alone.

## Tests

4137 Rust lib + architecture suite, full JS suite, clippy `--all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings`, fmt, `gen:ipc:check` + `gen:prompts:check`, eslint root + a11y — all green on the combined tree. Zero new dependencies.

title: fix: generation-burst reliability and the silent defects from the 2026-08-08 diagnostics bundle
body:
Everything here comes from one support bundle (`ajh-diagnostics-2026-08-08`, app 0.134.3): six applications imported, six résumé + cover-letter generations fired within 62 seconds on `ollama-cloud` / `gpt-oss:20b`.

## What the log actually showed

| run | started  | outcome                                    |
| --- | -------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| 1   | 19:56:14 | done — 8m37s                               |
| 2   | 19:56:32 | **failed — HTTP 429 after 8m55s**          |
| 3   | 19:56:43 | done — 11m28s                              |
| 4   | 19:56:51 | done — 13m14s                              |
| 5   | 19:57:09 | done — 12m44s                              |
| 6   | 19:57:16 | done — 11m40s                              |

**Peak 7 concurrent AI streams** against a documented cap of 3. The same workload on `gemma4:31b` earlier that day took 12–23 _seconds_ per run; `gpt-oss:20b` emitted 1,039,821 chars of reasoning against 45,416 of answer (22.9:1).

Worse than the one visible failure: **all six cover letters were written for a nonsense company** (`You'll Do` ×3, `experience **fast`, `the core of their product. You'll sit at the intersection of design`, `a **bootstrapped AI platform and consulting studio** based in Munich`) and **all six had zero company research**. None of it surfaced — the 27,601-line log contained exactly one `ERROR`, and 27,178 lines were a single repeated Tauri warning.

## Commits

| commit     | what                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ac8e0205` | Company name: the fallback regex alternated on a bare `at` with no word boundary, matching inside "Wh**at** You'll Do". `sanitizeCompanyName` now gates both the model's JSON and the regex; the bare `catch {}` that hid which ran is a warn.                       |
| `5074e14e` | **The concurrency cap was enforced on `ai_generate`, which the tailoring flow doesn't call.** `generate_pipeline` acquired nothing — no rate window, no slot, no daily charge. Now takes a slot via a new `acquire_queued` that waits rather than rejects, on the same semaphore. The renderer re-arms its deadline while queued. |
| `fc5863a0` | Research was bounded by a flat 25s around search **and** synthesis — a cap on how much reasoning the model was allowed. Now scales by effort off the same table `stream_deadline` uses. `salary_research` had the identical copy.                                    |
| `ece8d890` | Failed spans logged at INFO; `[ai] →`/`←` had nothing to pair them; 98.5% of the bundle was Tauri's stale-callback warning (one per streamed delta).                                                                                                                |
| `f34bf4c9` | Every HTTP 400 was `qwen3-embedding:8b` on `/api/chat`. `reachable_chat_model` returned `/api/tags`'s first entry — it was a health probe reused as "give me a chat model".                                                                                          |
| `80ace1b5` | A stream's initial 429 was never retried, on the reasoning that "a mid-stream restart duplicates deltas" — but the status arrives before any delta.                                                                                                                 |
| `75e07dc7` | Role extraction searched for `Jetzt bewerben` and `[← Alle offenen Stellen](/karriere)`. Also fixes the Rust twin of the `at` bug.                                                                                                                                  |
| `dd727531` | 1,932 rejected handshakes × 2 log lines each; `crashes.log` entries truncated mid-backtrace.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `b41de019` | A reasoning-heavy run now says so instead of looking hung.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## Verified

`cargo test --all-features` (3265) · `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets` clean · all 18 architecture rules · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0` · `pnpm test` (5014).

Every guard added here is mutation-tested — neutering `QueueSlot::drop`, leaking a permit, dropping the timeout re-arm, removing the chat-model filter, removing the log suppression, and removing the ratio check each fail a test.

## Not fixed, deliberately

- The `cannot move state from Destroyed` panic is third-party teardown I could not reproduce; a speculative guard would be worse than the next real backtrace, which is now capturable.
- The extension's ~10s reconnect is correct behaviour — browsers don't expose a failed WS handshake's HTTP status, so it genuinely cannot tell "refused" from "not running". Only the logging changed.

## Review notes

- `commands/ai.rs` and `ai_provider/mod.rs` were both at the R8 LOC cap, so this extracts `admit_research` (the ~40-line preamble three research commands repeated verbatim) and moves `RequestTrace` to its own module. Both are pure extractions.
- The architecture test caught an L2→L3 import in my first attempt at the research deadline; it's now injected by the L3 caller, matching how `SalaryResearch::enrich` already takes its cache.
- Pushed with `--no-verify` at the author's request, so the pre-push AI review gate did not run; the checks listed above were run manually.

title: feat: add exa as a fallback web-search backend for company research
body:
Company research ran on **the active AI provider's own web search**, which left a whole population with nothing:

- **`openai-compatible` gateways** report `supports_web_search: false` — every LM Studio / vLLM / OpenRouter / Groq / Together / DeepSeek user got no research at all.
- **Local Ollama** reports `supports_web_search: true` for the _family_, but the Ollama Web Search API needs a separate **ollama.com account key**. A keyless install showed the "search company" toggle **ON** and returned an empty brief every single time.

The second is worse, because nothing surfaced it. The 2026-08-08 bundle that drove #960 showed the cost: six cover letters written with no company knowledge, indistinguishable from six written with a full brief — plus 28 lifetime `no usable brief (provider found nothing)` lines no user would ever see.

## The seam already existed

`research.rs` was already provider-agnostic (the `SearchResult` shape, query builders, synthesis prompts, injection guard), and the three `ollama_research*` functions were each:

```
search → if empty return "" → synthesize with the provider's own model
```

**Only the search step was ever Ollama-specific.** So this is a search-backend swap, not a new research pipeline.

## What changed

| commit     | what                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `efd0c974` | `WebSearcher` trait + `ExaSearcher` (`api.exa.ai/search`, `ai:exa`). The three pipelines move to `search/` as `searched_research*`, so company / salary / per-question answers all gain the fallback at once.               |
| `1414c4a0` | `supportsWebSearch` reports whether research can actually **run**, not what the provider advertises. Plus the Exa key slot in Settings → Company Research.                                                                   |
| `d50f536e` | ADR-0023, the **search backend** glossary term, README/SECURITY egress enumeration, and two already-stale fixes in `anti-abuse-limits.md`.                                                                                  |

## Three decisions, each with a real alternative

1. **Fallback only, resolved from configuration before any call.** A provider that can already search keeps its own search *even with an Exa key stored* — nobody silently starts paying a second vendor. `resolve_search_backend` is a pure predicate so the rule is pinned by a test, not convention; inverting it fails that test.
2. **No second chance.** A native search that runs and returns empty is not retried against Exa. It would rescue the 28 observed empty briefs, but costs a second billable call on every miss and lets two vendors see one query.
3. **Synthesis stays on the user's own model.** Exa's `/answer` would be fewer calls but bypasses both `SYNTH_SYSTEM`'s prompt-injection guard (search results are attacker-reachable text, and this is the one stage that reads them unfenced) and the `is_no_info` filter.

The fallback lands on the `AiProvider::research` **default**, so providers with native search override it and are untouched, and a new provider with no search inherits it — no per-provider change either way.

## Behaviour change worth a release note

A keyless Ollama user who sees the research toggle **ON** today will see it **OFF** after this. That is the bug being fixed — the toggle was promising a brief it could never produce — but it is visible.

## Egress

No ADR-0005 amendment. Exa is a new _vendor_ inside the already-enumerated **class 3 (web search, opt-in)**, not a new egress class, and it is opt-in by construction — nothing is sent until a key is stored. It receives exactly what the current search already does (company name, role title, question topic); never résumés, generations, applications or credentials. Rust-side via `net::http`, so no CSP change. Exa charges its own `(day, vendor)` daily bucket rather than spending the AI provider's.

## Verified

`cargo fmt --check` · `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets` clean · `cargo test --all-features` (3277, incl. all 18 architecture rules) · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0` · `pnpm format:check` · `pnpm test` (5028).

Mutation-checked: making `resolve_search_backend` prefer Exa fails the fallback-only test.

## Review notes

- `ai_provider/mod.rs` sits at the R8 LOC cap, so the new code is its own module; the two new trait methods carry deliberately tight docs to stay under it.
- One thing this PR does **not** do: surface Exa's `costDollars` (returned per response) into the spend store. The store is token-shaped and a real per-search cost deserves its own change.

title: fix: link orphaned landing routes from home and add sitemap lastmod
body:
## Why

Search Console (Aug 8, 2026) flagged `aijobhunter.app`: 4 indexed / 18 not indexed. Most of the 18 are benign — http→https and www→apex redirects, `?ref=` variants covered by canonical, and Cloudflare's `/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection` 404. The real signal is five pages Google will not serve:

| URL | State |
| --- | --- |
| `/accessibility`, `/agent-system`, `/architecture-map`, `/how-it-works` | Discovered – currently not indexed, **last crawled `N/A`** |
| `/world` | Crawled, not indexed (WebGL page, near-zero text — expected) |
| `/tech-radar` | Not in any Search Console bucket yet |

Nothing was blocking them: all return 200, none carry `noindex`, `robots.txt` is `Allow: /`, and the sitemap reads Success (10 URLs, last read Aug 8).

## What

**1. Home footer had drifted from the doc-page footer.** `SiteFooter` links `/agent-system`, `/architecture-map`, `/tech-radar` and `/storybook/`; the home `Finale` foot-nav did not. Those routes were reachable only from pages Google has not fetched yet, so they sat one hop behind an uncrawled page — and `/` is the only URL on this domain with real crawl equity. Same orphan class #934 fixed for `/how-it-works`.

**2. `HomeBody.test.tsx` asserts the invariant**: every sitemap route (except `/`) is linked from home. Mutation-checked — removing any one link fails it.

**3. Sitemap entries carry `lastmod`**, hand-kept from each route's last content-bearing commit rather than a build timestamp. A fresh date on every deploy is exactly the churn Google learns to distrust; too-old is the safe failure direction.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @ajh/landing test` — 338 passed (37 files)
- `pnpm lint:strict` clean · `tsc --noEmit` clean
- Built `out/sitemap.xml` carries `<lastmod>`; built `out/index.html` links all 10 routes
- Pre-push gate: parity OK, agent-system in sync, AI review clean

Indexing is still gated on crawl budget for a young domain — the remaining lever is **Request indexing** per URL in Search Console, which is a manual step on the account.

title: feat: deterministic content validation and quality report for generated documents
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the multi-stage resume pipeline programme: every generated résumé and cover letter is now **deterministically validated against the candidate's own source document**, with the result persisted, surfaced in the UI, and available to the agent. The core rule made mechanical: the LLM decides HOW to present verified evidence — these validators catch it deciding WHAT.

- **`validate/content/`** (L1): 25-code deterministic validator family — factual (unsourced metrics/terms/dates, dropped roles, altered project links), alignment (coverage regression vs source, missing evidenced requirements), consistency (dates, title drift, skills claimed-but-not-demonstrated, project-structure tiers), duplicates, ATS structure + keyword-density, and a `voice.*` anti-AI-tell family (single-source lexicon shared with the generation prompts via codegen). Criticals come only from deterministic checks — a model can never emit one.
- **`documents/evidence.rs`** (L1): evidence extraction (`extract_evidence`/`rank_bullets`) — the `rank_trim_candidates` core moved out of the R8-frozen `match_resume.rs` (net −141 lines, trim-panel wire-compat pinned by test).
- **`quality_report` on `ai_generations`** (ADR-007 §F2): opaque wrapper JSON, per-top-level-key merge, full backup/restore round-trip, 256 KB clamps on both write paths.
- **`resume:validateContent` IPC** (5-step): server-side clamps, strict docKind, content-free spans (ADR-027).
- **Four agent Read tools**: `validate_resume`, `search_candidate_evidence`, `lookup_salary`, `get_trim_suggestions` — fenced, clamped, least-privilege-pinned; fence-tag registry + `tool_result` marker hardened against forgery (incl. nested-marker bypass).
- **`pnpm gen:prompts` codegen**: the anti-AI-tell lexicon is generated from `natural-voice.ts` into Rust with a CI drift gate — one source instructs the model and validates its output, guarded in both directions.
- **Renderer**: integrity badge + QualityReportPanel (evidence-first, guidance-framed, en+de), report-carrying saves, staleness via source-text hash, Re-check action, hand-edit nudge.

## Review trail

Five domain critics + a security review + a 3-pass `/review` ensemble with per-finding fresh-context verification ran before this PR. Every blocking finding was fixed with mutation-verified regression tests, including: six false-positive Criticals on truthful documents, a per-key merge defect, a forged-fence-tag hole, a renderer cancel race, a UTF-8 boundary panic on accented URLs (`café-berlin.de`) that would have aborted the app mid-generation, and a malformed-persisted-report renderer crash. Zero verifier-rejected findings; ledger updated.

## Test plan

- `cargo test --lib`: 3410 passed · `--test architecture`: 18/18 · clippy `-D warnings` clean
- Desktop vitest: 3074 passed · prompts 742 · workspace typecheck 13/13 · `lint:strict` clean
- `gen:ipc:check` + `gen:prompts:check` clean · backup/export round-trip covers the new column
- Fixtures include paraphrased-but-truthful en+de documents (zero-Critical guards) and accented-URL project entries

title: feat: native structured output for openai, gemini and ollama with a hardened json parse module
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 (structured-output half) of the multi-stage résumé pipeline programme: `complete_structured(app, req, schema_hint)` on the `AiProvider` trait with a prompt-discipline default, native overrides where the wire format is verified, and a pure, hardened JSON extraction/repair/parse module for the pipeline stages that will consume it. This is deliberate forward surface — zero production callers yet; `Completer::complete_json` (which must charge `record_usage` itself) wires it up in the next phase.

- **openai** — `response_format: json_schema` (strict mode) via new `openai_body.rs`; schema `strictify` with depth cap and whole-degrade to `json_object` on composition keywords it can't walk
- **gemini** — `responseSchema` translation via new `gemini_body.rs`; kept-keyword set verified against the current Schema reference (incl. `pattern`, `minimum`/`maximum`, length/property bounds); degrades to `responseMimeType` + hint when a schema can't be translated whole
- **ollama** — native `format` field; **ollama_cloud** delegates through the OpenAI-compatible layer (`response_format` support cited to vendor docs)
- **anthropic** — deliberately NO override: older models take the prompt-discipline default; no guessed beta wire format
- **`pipeline/json.rs`** — candidate-ordered `extract`/`repair`/`parse<T>`: whole-response first, fenced bodies last-first, balanced spans last-first, containment-aware repair ordering, content-free `Display`/`Debug` on the error type, ADR-010-fenced `reask_detail()`
- `req.effort` threads through all three native structured paths using the same per-provider gates as the streaming bodies
- `pagination.rs` split out of `ai_provider/mod.rs` (mechanical); dead `supportsStructuredOutput` flag removed from `packages/prompts` + renderer + docs

## Internal review (pre-PR gates)

- `tauri-security-reviewer` (BLOCK → fixed): fence-inside-string-value extraction hijack, `Debug` leaking withheld model content (Sentry-reachable), provenance-dropping prompt join, unfenced re-ask detail, case-sensitive role match, unbounded schema recursion — all reproduced red first, fixed, mutation-checked
- 3-pass `pr-reviewer` ensemble (opus + 2× sonnet) + verification: 7 further findings fixed (containment-aware repair ordering incl. executed PoCs, sibling anti-decoy pinning test, effort threading, strict-mode composition-keyword degrade on both translators, Gemini constraint keywords, empty-hint directive, `extract_json` trap removal)
- cleanup audit: zero dead code; one doc drift fixed (`ARCHITECTURE.md` provider-profile description)

## Gates

`cargo fmt` · `clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings` · `cargo test --all-features --lib` (3626) · `--test architecture` (18) · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint:strict` · `@ajh/prompts` vitest (750) — all green.

title: feat(pipeline): phase 3 — the quality generation depth
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of the multi-stage résumé pipeline: the **Quality** generation depth, end to end. A quality run analyzes the job ad, grounds evidence against the source résumé, plans a strategy on the seeded role roster, streams a draft, validates it deterministically, and repairs failing sections — then presents an integrity report with per-bullet fabrication review. The fast path is byte-identical and remains the default.

### Rust spine
- `pipeline/resume/`: six stages behind `Pipeline::run_hooked`; flat serde artifact types with filled examples; ADR-017 stage caching (`PIPELINE_PROMPT_VERSION`-pinned); prompts interpolate the generated `prompt_blocks` consts.
- **The core rule is structural, not prompted**: evidence quotes are verbatim-filtered with status overwritten from the keywords kernel; the strategy is rebuilt on the roster seeded from the parsed résumé (the model authors only angle/emphasis, filtered against grounded evidence); every Critical is deterministic; roles can never be dropped.
- Repair ≤2 rounds, section-scoped splice, reverts when strictly worse; the run deadline is enforced between stages, between repair rounds, AND between per-section calls.
- `commands/resume_pipeline`: five commands; `RunHooks` is the sole emit/persist/stop point; terminal state derives status+reason together (a failed run can never report "done"); terminal notifications via the Notification Center.
- **Retry infrastructure hardening** (found by the review chain): `send_with_retry`/`send_stream_with_retry` now own the per-request timeout as a total budget — a "300s" call can no longer run 900s through retries; embeds get a dedicated sequence budget preserving cold-model-load recovery; a sub-RTT doomed attempt is refused so the actionable 429 survives.
- **Fence primitive hardening** (three review iterations, all executed evidence): attribute-form tags neutralized, kept runs have inner `<` broken (same-tag nesting cannot reconstitute a boundary), legitimate multi-line content preserved.

### Renderer
- Run machine + session hook: terminal detection reads the run record (a cancel/deadline stop emits no stage event — discovered and contract-documented); the mid-run `job_complete` trap is test-pinned; a failed first fetch surfaces an error instead of a dead poll.
- Depth selection (Settings default + per-run override, self-describing popover with honest cost numbers, en+de), staged GeneratingPanel, section verdict chips, runs list, and the **fabrication review**: a verdict is intent, the document is fact — Remove applies the edit through the surface's own editor (anchored on the exact line the report carries; refuses without an anchor), and an entry only counts resolved when verdict and document agree.
- Entry point on the job detail pane (`TailoredResumePanel`): fast routes to the existing tailor flow; quality invokes the pipeline with server-resolved identities.

### Agent tools + docs
- Three Read tools: `analyze_job`, `get_quality_report` (both prep-flow), `run_quality_pipeline` (gated to the Phase-7 flow — the 360s step-timeout arithmetic, pinned in tests, forbids it in prep). Saving stays behind the gated `save_resume`.
- ADR-032 (pipeline ownership + mechanical rule enforcement), ADR-033 (no model-written agent memory); domain docs updated; the two source specs rewritten as repo-aware briefs.

## Review chain (pre-PR)

Eight internal rounds: spine → architect BLOCK (3H) + security (1H) → fixes → delta BLOCK (retry-multiplier 3× understatement) → fixes → consensus fence CRITICAL (executed) → fixes → renderer critics (trust-integrity HIGH: Remove-then-green; contrast; poll death) → fixes → wiring rounds → final 3-pass ensemble + scoped security pass (2 HIGH: triple-confirmed stale-cache writable lock; substring deletion eating the contact header — both fixed with regression fixtures). ~90 findings total, every fix mutation-verified, several reviewer-prescribed fixes probed and disproven with executed evidence before better fixes shipped.

title: feat(pipeline): phase 4 — the max generation depth
body:
Phase 4 of the staged résumé pipeline: the **max** generation depth — per-section generation over the strategy roster, a code-owned assemble step, an LLM judge, per-entry regenerate, and the live section timeline. Follows #968 (run infra) and #969 (quality depth).

## What max depth does

- **Per-section generation** (`stages/section_gen.rs`): sequential structured calls per section — Summary → Skills → one call per `CompanyPlan` (8-company cap + the condensed "Earlier roles" group, roster seeded by strategy) → Projects → Education. Identity (company/title/dates) is **seeded, never model-authored**: `ExperienceOut` has no identity fields to rename an employer with, and `ProjectsOut` seeds name/links/stack verbatim (3-tier degradation ladder). Evidence citations (`used_evidence`) are filtered against the grounded map — invented citations are dropped, never repaired.
- **Assemble** (`assemble.rs`, pure): renders the same plain-text body shape the quality draft produces, so the editor / report / repair / export pipeline downstream is unchanged. Section order from strategy is applied as a **kind-block permutation** (an employment group moves as one unit under one heading). Header excluded (ADR-0021).
- **Judge** (`stages/llm_judge`, runs LAST after repair): one structured call reviewing the finished document; items are structurally Warning-only (`JudgeItem` has no severity field), quote-verified verbatim, capped, and merged under `judge.*` codes the renderer labels as AI-reviewer provenance. Skippable — any failure records `{skipped, reasonCode}` and the run continues.
- **Per-entry regenerate**: `experience:<i>` rebuilds one roster entry from the persisted strategy/evidence artifacts, joined on the **full seeded identity triple** (company + title + dates — an employer name is not a key), splices atomically with a fresh report, and degrades to the whole-section repair path on any miss.
- **Artifacts + retention**: full strategy/evidence artifacts persist in `pipeline_run_events` at max depth only (log lines stay counts-only per ADR-027). Both delete doors cascade: application delete and generation delete purge the run trail; `job_url` is normalized at every boundary including restore.
- **Save gate**: a draft that lost the source's work history never overwrites the saved résumé — the gate compares the artifacts (source vs draft), not the run's control-flow signals.
- **Repair rule change (both depths)**: a repair round that *introduces* an absence-shaped Critical (a dropped role, a lost source project link) is reverted regardless of critical counts — the pure-count rule accepted trades that deleted employers.
- **Renderer**: max selectable end-to-end (Settings default + per-run override), live `SectionTimeline` with a per-section screen-reader announcer, progressive document assembly over the existing display-only stream, judge provenance badges, deadline table codegen'd (`MAX_RUN_FIXED_SECS` now emitted by gen-ipc beside the quality pair).

## Budget

Max ≈ 24 flat-bounded calls: fixed deadline 7 200 s + one effort-scaled pass (7 500–8 100 s by tier), `Budget::RESUME_MAX.run_timeout` 125 min, renderer bound strictly above backend at every tier (lock-tested both sides). Every call charges the daily cap; the deadline is checked between section calls, and zero-provider-cost stages (assemble/validate) may complete after a deadline stop so paid work is never discarded.

title: test(pipeline): phase 5 — the offline eval harness
body:
Phase 5 of the staged résumé pipeline: the **offline eval harness** — the measurement layer that gates judge expansion, `factual.unsourced_term` W→C escalation, and further depth investment. Follows #970 (max depth).

## What it does

- **`tests/eval.rs`** grows from the Phase-1 corpus-shape stub into the real harness: every labelled fixture under `validate/content/fixtures/` (7 planted defects, 5 truthful, 2 tolerated degradations, en+de) runs through the same `validate_content` entry point the product calls, producing a per-code precision/recall table. Reuses the product fixtures — no parallel corpus.
- **Labels are guards, not decoration**: planted codes are asserted found at their registered severity (a Critical→Warning demotion must be acknowledged in the label), Planted fixtures may not raise Criticals nobody planted, truthful *and* tolerated fixtures are pinned to zero Criticals, and a `case!` macro binds each row's file name to its `include_str!` path so they cannot disagree. A two-way coverage invariant means a new fixture cannot sit ungraded and a stale row cannot grade nothing.
- **The headline is honest**: the Warning-tier false-positive budget counts *findings* (not distinct codes — the letter fixture fires 16 warnings from 2 codes), is asserted (`0` today), and prints its own caveat: 2 of the 5 truthful fixtures are already pinned empty by unit tests, so only 3 can move.   • The new address format for the config-file input that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 is now enabled by default. All previous input formats continue to be accepted as well. #4023
  • The CodeQL Action can now make use of configured private registries in Default Setup to retrieve CodeQL configuration files from remote repositories that require authentication. This will allow customers to store their CodeQL configuration in a single repository that can then be referenced by Default Setup workflows in other repositories. We expect to roll this and other, related changes out to everyone in July. #4007

4.37.1 - 16 Jul 2026

4.37.0 - 08 Jul 2026

All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

4.36.3 - 01 Jul 2026

No user facing changes.

  • Cache CodeQL CLI version information across Actions steps. #3943
  • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937

title: feat(pipeline): phase 6 — per-stage models and the local-model advisor
body:
Phase 6 of the staged résumé pipeline: **per-stage AI models + the local-model advisor**. Follows #971 (eval harness).

## What it does

- **Per-stage model overrides**: each paying pipeline stage (analyze → evidence → strategy → draft/sections → repair → judge) can run on its own provider+model, stored in a new `ai_stage_overrides` table on the AI config store (append-only migration), resolved through `Completer::from_active_for_stage` with the exact same validate/SSRF chain as the active config. Free stages (assemble/validate) are rejected at write, import, and read — the reject set is codegen'd from the pipeline truth (`PIPELINE_STAGES_FREE`) so it cannot drift. **No per-stage `base_url` exists, structurally**: security review showed an accepted-but-undisplayed egress field is a covert channel even when validated, so the column was removed and resolve-time follows the one URL Settings displays.
- **Per-stage cache keys**: `StageCacheKey` now carries provider+model+context_window per stage (`StageIdentity`) — two configs differing in one stage's override cache separately for that stage and share everything else. The window joined the key because it changes what the model sees (`num_ctx`), the review's "clean regression" catch.
- **Context-window threading**: the user's configured window now reaches staged Ollama calls (it previously reached only the fast path — every staged run silently used the 2048 default). Bounds enforced at write, patch, import, resolve, and both wire entrypoints. A one-shot backfill promotes existing installs' configured windows so the fix reaches upgrading users, not just new ones.
- **PATCH provider settings**: `set_provider_settings` is now non-destructive on absence server-side (absent = keep, explicit null = clear, value = set) — the old REPLACE contract had already silently erased fields at three call sites.
- **Settings UI**: a per-stage overrides card (effective model per stage, plain-language stage descriptions, card-level vs per-row warnings), a suggested-smaller-model banner for the extraction stages (measured `parameterSize` on both sides required — never the tier fallback; one-click accept, never silent), and a 4-step **Model advisor** wizard: installed models → context-fit against the real stage prompt budgets → recommendations (app-does-this vs advice-you-run-yourself, strictly separated) → thinking-model risk (spend-store data where providers report it, honest "not measured ≠ safe" copy elsewhere).
- **Spend store**: `thinking_tokens` column recorded where providers genuinely report the split (OpenAI `reasoning_tokens`, Gemini `thoughtsTokenCount`); NULL elsewhere — absence of data is never presented as absence of risk.
- **Restore resilience**: one malformed row (or entry) in a backup's provider/override maps is dropped per-row instead of failing the whole section restore — tolerance at both the type and entry level, probed with `-1`, `2^32`, wrong-typed and string entries.

## Review provenance

Seven internal rounds before this PR: ai-provider-expert (BLOCK → fix → delta APPROVE → advisories), frontend-reviewer + ui-ux-expert on the renderer (both BLOCK: the suggestion heuristic recommending a 70B/embedding model as "smaller", measured AA contrast failures, a modal focus escape — all fixed with executed evidence), tauri-security-reviewer (APPROVE + the covert-channel finding that removed the per-stage base_url), and a 3-pass ensemble (BLOCK → 4 HIGHs fixed, incl. a 3-pass-consensus ref-scoping bug in the window-commit latch and the missing upgrade backfill). ~100 findings closed across the rounds, all red-first with executed mutations; reviewer prescriptions disproven and corrected in both directions along the way.

## Tests

4049 Rust lib + 18 architecture; renderer vitest 3471+ (incl. new StageOverrideEditor / LocalModelLimits / ModelAdvisor suites); i18n en+de key resolution executed against the real i18next instance; clippy `--all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings`, fmt, gen:ipc drift gate, lint:strict + a11y lint — all green. Zero new dependencies; lockfiles unchanged.

Rider: a one-line structural read fixes the pre-existing `router-guard.ts` TanStack type drift that blocked the frontend typecheck gate (present on main).

title: fix(autopilot): stop the double scroll when returning from an application
body:
Fixes the owner-reported jump on the Autopilot page: with several autopilots and the bottom one expanded, applying to a job and then clicking **Back to autopilot** produced two visible motions — the router's global scroll-restoration pass fired first (reset/restore over the whole list), then the page's own focus effect suddenly centered the previously-expanded autopilot.

## What changed

- **One clean scroll.** The application page's `back()` now passes `resetScroll: false` to `navigate()` for the return-to-autopilot trip, so TanStack Router's restore-and-reset pass (verified against the installed `@tanstack/router-core@1.171.21` source — the flag gates the whole block, restoration included) is skipped exactly where the Autopilot page's existing pending-focus effect takes over and performs the single centered scroll it always did.
- **The skip is gated structurally, not by origin alone.** `from=autopilot` is a URL search param that outlives the one-shot in-memory pending-focus state (native forward-nav can replay it), so the gate reads the session store at call time: `resetScroll: !(from === 'autopilot' && hasPendingAutopilotFocus)`. A stale `?from=autopilot` with no pending focus falls back to the router's default reset instead of silently dropping all motion.
- Other back origins (`jobs`, `applications`, none) keep the default reset-to-top — they have no compensating scroll effect.

## Review provenance

frontend-reviewer APPROVE: it read the router package source to confirm the `resetScroll` semantics claim, live-mutated the gate to confirm the seam tests go red, and surfaced the origin-vs-state correlation gap that the second commit closes (plus a comment documenting the trust boundary where backend-supplied search params reach `navigate()`).

Seam-level (jsdom zeroes rects, so the tests pin the `navigate()` call shape, not pixels): `from='autopilot'` with pending focus → `resetScroll: false`; without → `true`; `jobs`/no-origin → `true`. title: feat(agent): phase 7 — the flow registry and the improve-resume flow
body:
Phase 7 of the staged résumé pipeline: the **agent flow registry** and its second flow, **improve_resume**. Follows #985 (per-stage models).

## What it does

- **`AgentFlow` + `FLOWS`** (`agent/flows.rs`): a flow is `{ kind, system, tools, budget, seeds_generation }` — prompt/whitelist/budget mismatch is now unrepresentable, and adding a flow forces every field at compile time. `kind` rides `AgentRunRequest` (serde-defaulted to `prep_application`); an unknown kind is a validation error, never a fallback, and the wire vocabulary is codegen'd + drift-tested from both sides.
- **The `improve_resume` flow**: reviews an existing tailored generation against its quality report + evidence and proposes targeted fixes; its only write is the gated `save_resume`. The whitelist is the Phase-3-shipped `improve_resume_tools()` (six tools, including `run_quality_pipeline`'s only home). The generation is loaded server-side and fenced — seed material is not a skippable tool call.
- **Fail-closed cap parity**: a generation longer than the 8k transcript seed is *refused at run start* rather than truncated — review found the round trip (8k seed → model "corrects" what it saw → 40k save overwrites the full document) would have been silent, irreversible tail loss that the existing `draftTruncated` guard structurally cannot catch. The cap is now a generated one-number property (`AGENT_RESUME_TEXT_CAP` → gen:ipc → `RESUME_CAP`), gating both the backend refusal and the UI's disabled-with-reason entry.
- **A fresh report on every save**: an approved improve save writes text + a recomputed quality report + a re-synced run status in one shape — review caught that it previously kept the old document's verdict forever. The rule is mechanical: a reportless save request refuses to build.
- **Per-call tool ceiling**: `max_tool_calls` is enforced *inside* the tool-call loop (providers emit parallel calls — a turn-boundary check bounded turns, not calls), giving `StoppedReason::MaxToolCalls` its first producer; calls past the ceiling get fenced error bodies, and a Write past the ceiling never suspends the run on a confirm the user shouldn't see.
- **`Budget::AGENT_IMPROVE`**: a 90-minute step clock sized so one full quality-pipeline pass (4500s deadline + one post-admission completion + margin) fits inside one step — with the honest doc that per-attempt-and-sequence HTTP timeouts bound every ordinary turn at 120–300s across all four adapters.
- **Renderer**: an "Improve this résumé" entry on the finished-generation panel (aria-disabled with visible reasons; too-long pre-check counts code points to match the backend exactly), a compact in-modal checklist card (a second dialog would trap the confirm behind an unreachable focus boundary), progress rows keyed on *executed evidence* — the confirm request is the proof a save was offered, so a ceiling-refused save reads "Not reached", never "Done" — a résumé editor in the confirm gate (content-only edited args), report writes locked during a live review (the pending save would overwrite them), and invalidation on approve so the payoff is visible immediately. en+de throughout, with the locale matrix executed against the real i18next.

## Review provenance

Seven internal rounds: architect + security spine reviews (both independently converged on the truncate-then-overwrite CRITICAL), a delta re-verify that caught the ceiling being enforced at the wrong loop boundary, frontend + UX renderer reviews (forever-stale panel after approve, focus escapes, ceiling rows lying), and a 3-pass ensemble (the write-lock gap, the stale-report save, a 3-pass-consensus tooltip regression from a mid-round recovery commit). ~50 findings, all closed red-first with executed mutations; three architect rulings recorded in-code (per-tool timeouts deferred with a named trigger condition; the generation lookup stays server-side; `seeds_generation` is a field so the compiler asks flow #3 the question).

title: feat(export): phase 8 — sidebar and monogram letter layouts, and a reachable letter ATS toggle
body:
Phase 8b of the staged résumé pipeline programme — the final phase: two new cover-letter layouts and the toggle that governs them. Follows #986 (agent flow registry).

## What it does

- **Sidebar** — a tinted contact rail down the left edge (name, role, contact stacked in the rail; body in its own column). The rail letterhead is **shrink-to-fit**: the widest unbreakable token is measured and the type stepped down (absolute 6 pt floor, itself measured — a percentage floor turned out to be *backwards*, flooring highest exactly on the large-name templates most at risk) so long surnames and emails never print into the gutter. The header documents honestly that the rail cannot coexist with DIN 5008 Form B's address window and points German window-envelope users to Classic/Navy.
- **Monogram** — an initials device in the header. The initials derivation refuses pronoun parentheticals ("(they/them)"), title abbreviations ("Dr.", "Dipl.-Ing." — while keeping "J. Smith" → JS), salutations, sign-offs, subject lines **and dates** ("12 March 2025" is not a person), with PDF and DOCX sharing the ONE guarded function — the unguarded variant is no longer exported.
- **Both layouts get DOCX approximations** (rail → cell shading, device → shaded run with its separator spaces deliberately *unshaded*), register at all six registration points, and **never hyphenate**: justify without `hyphenate: false` emits U+00AD soft hyphens straight into the extracted text layer. A roster guard pins both new layouts; sweeping the four shipped layouts is a parked follow-up (needs a justify-vs-rivers decision for German plus preview churn).
- **The cover-letter ATS toggle is finally reachable.** The Rust path always read `data.opts.ats` for letters, but no letter surface exposed the switch and five sites force-cleared the flag under ATS-tier résumé templates — a Monogram + ATS-tier combination shipped decoration with *no off switch* while the en/de copy promised one. Now: a shared `AtsModeToggle` renders at all three surfaces that pick letter layouts, gated by a `LETTER_LAYOUT_DECORATED` registry that mirrors the `.typ` ats gates one-for-one (a new layout id fails `tsc` until someone decides). One decision function (`shouldClearAtsMode`) governs both template *and* layout changes — including releasing the flag in cover-only runs, where the résumé template's tier is irrelevant.

title: fix: make a failed generation visible instead of silently resetting
body:
Follow-up to #958. Three fixes, all about a generation failing without telling anyone.

## 1. A failed tailored generation silently reset to the wizard

`TailorFlow` derives its stage as `generating → done if there is output → else configuring`. A failed run leaves both outputs empty, so it fell back to the wizard — and the file contained **zero references to `error`**. `runTailor` wrote the message to the session, the hook returned it, nothing rendered it, and the catch only `console.error`d, so there was no toast either. The result was a generation that appeared to do nothing at all, which cost two investigations to reproduce.

Returning to the wizard is right — the user needs to change something and retry — but it has to arrive with the reason. The error now renders below the wizard where the user just clicked Generate, and a toast fires, matching what the AI Generate wizard already did. The toast carries a fixed translated string; the raw provider message goes in the panel, not a transient toast.

The test drives a real failure through the hook and asserts the rendered text rather than the store field — a test that only checked the field was set would have passed against the broken code, which is how this survived.

## 2. The stream deadline was not scaled by reasoning effort

300 s, hardcoded on both the Rust and renderer sides. `reqwest`'s `RequestBuilder::timeout` bounds the **whole** request — connect through the last streamed byte — so a generation that legitimately runs longer is killed mid-stream. High effort on a large cloud model with a full résumé plus job ad sits squarely in that range, and is the likely throw behind the failure in §1.

Both sides now scale by the request's effort, with the renderer as the outer bound so the backend's actionable provider error fires first rather than a generic renderer timeout. The tables can't be shared across the IPC boundary, so a test hardcodes the backend schedule and asserts the renderer exceeds it at every tier.

**Worth flagging:** the tier order is the vendors' — `max` sits **above** `xhigh` (Anthropic's effort docs, OpenAI's `reasoning_effort`). That reads wrong at a glance and was inverted in the first cut, giving the highest-effort runs the *shortest* deadline. Both monotonicity tests listed the tiers in that same wrong order, so they passed against it; only the value assertions caught it. Both tables and both arrays now carry a comment saying why the order is what it is.

Rejected alternative: a per-chunk idle timeout would be architecturally nicer, but it would mean loosening the total timeout at all four call sites plus a second timing mechanism inside the shared stream loop — and it wouldn't need effort-awareness at all. Documented in `timeouts.rs`.

## 3. A truncated generation was saved as complete

`finish()` consulted `stop_reason` only inside the `is_empty` branch, so a stream that emitted text and then reported `finish_reason: "length"` took the success path: terminal event, `job_complete`, persisted result. A truncated résumé or cover letter was saved and exported as if finished. `parse_openai_finish_reason` already produced `StopReason::Length`; it was simply unused on the non-empty path.

It still completes and still keeps the partial text — that text is worth having, and this must not be fatal — but it now raises a notification through the existing Notification Center (the same seam `email_watch_scheduler` and `reminder_scheduler` use) rather than presenting a cut-off document as done.

## 4. Carried over from #958

`gemini_is_recognized_pre_v3` additionally required a `gemini-` prefix, so a `gemma-*` or `learnlm-*` id — which Google's listing surfaces, since `parse_model_page` filters on `models/` and not on family — got a fully neutral profile while every other gate in that file keys only on the v3 boundary. The gate is now the exact inversion of the v3 check. Confirmed while there that the v3 check cannot misclassify a Gemma id: it requires the literal prefix before parsing any version digits.

## Testing

`cargo test --all-features` (incl. architecture) · renderer suite · `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -D warnings` · `cargo fmt`.

Note: this was pushed with `--no-verify` at the author's request, so the pre-push gate did not run. The full `pnpm test` / `typecheck` / `lint:strict` sweep is CI's here rather than local.

title: fix: stop the resume prompt licensing invented metrics, and let each provider own its sampling
body:
Two related changes to generation quality, folded together because the second depends on the first.

## 1. Prompt contradictions

Prompt sizes were **measured** with a real tokenizer before anything was touched — résumé 4,563 tokens, analyze 5,684, cover letter 4,058. Size was never the problem and nothing was rewritten for it. `locale/index.ts` is 973 lines and contributes 40 tokens per request; `links.ts` is 1,221 lines and contributes 0. The defect was contradiction density in the `full` tier of two files.

**The résumé prompt licensed inventing metrics.** It said *"NEVER fabricate numbers - only use metrics if they're in the original **or can be reasonably inferred**"*, two lines after mandating that every bullet carry a measurable result, with ATS mode adding "quantify every achievement" — while three other rules in the same prompt banned exactly what that clause permits. The `brief` tier and the Rust port of the same spine both got it right, so the `full` tier, the one cloud users hit, was the outlier. A résumé with an invented number is one the candidate has to defend in an interview.

**The analyze prompt fought itself over keyword matching.** *"Synonyms fail 70% of the time"* and *"Hard Skills: Must match EXACTLY"*, then 150 lines later *"React.js = React = ReactJS"* — while the user prompt and the Rust `SYNONYMS` map both implement semantic matching. That decides `missingKeywords` and `keywordCoverage`, which the user sees. The ATS score was also decomposed two incompatible ways in one system prompt.

Also removed: ~500 tokens instructing a weighted `overall` score that has no field in the schema (only `overallAssessment: string`), a `### CANDIDATE RESUME ###` header emitted ~170 lines after the résumé it announces, a leaked `topRequirements` variable name, and a duplicate point budget. The German subject label now goes through the output-language fitter like the salutation and sign-off already did, the format skeleton gains the subject slot it mandates, and the company-research sentences are gated on a brief actually being fenced.

Deliberately **not** touched: the step-by-step scaffolding. It is test-gated and its benefit was the one thing the audit could not verify empirically.

## 2. Sampling ownership

The renderer picked a temperature per task step and sent it to whatever model was configured. That is wrong on most of them now:

- Non-default `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k` returns **400 on every request** to Claude 4.7+, thinking or not.
- OpenAI reasoning models reject `temperature`.
- Google says to remove the parameters from Gemini 3 requests entirely, and documents that below 1.0 causes looping.
- Six of eight families publish one number per model with **no task dimension at all**, so the per-step table was tuning an axis no vendor supports.

Gemini already had a guard for this and it was dead code: it withheld the adapter's fallback only when the caller supplied nothing, but the renderer always supplied something, so every request looked like a deliberate user choice. The onboarding default is a Gemini 3 model, so new users hit the documented degradation case on their first generation.

The renderer now sends an **intent** and each adapter owns the numbers, behind a trait method beside `effort_levels`. Explicit values still win, so the per-model temperature sliders keep working. Anthropic needed no behavioural change — its fail-safe was already right, and the work was generalising it to the other four adapters.

### The correction that mattered

The first cut defaulted every adapter to sending nothing, on the theory that omitting is neutral. **It is not.** Omitting means the model applies its own default, which is 0.7–1.0. Measured against the live local Ollama on the author's machine:

```
qwen3.6:27b-q4_K_M   → temperature 1, presence_penalty 1.5, top_p 0.95
gemma4:31b-it-q4_K_M → temperature 1
```

So on a default local install the résumé surface would have run at 1.0 **with `presence_penalty 1.5`** — the exact knob that pushes a model toward new topics — partly undoing the prompt hardening in the same branch. Omission is right only where sending is refused or documented-harmful; everywhere else each adapter declares values reproducing today's behaviour. Anthropic and Ollama were reading the request directly and never consulted their own profile, which is what kept Anthropic's hardcoded `unwrap_or(0.7)` invisible.

Also fixed: the cover letter moves to the grounded profile (calling it "creative" was an argument about temperature, not about a penalty that rewards new topics in a letter asserting real achievements to an employer); inline rewrite returns to deterministic; the OpenAI-compatible adapter no longer hands OpenAI's numbers to arbitrary gateways; and the job analysis and inline rewrite now route through the resolver — both used bare literals, so the Settings "analysis" slider changed metadata extraction and not the analysis it is named for.

## Testing

Tests assert the **request body**, per adapter, per intent, including the absences — because the previous round asserted the intent string and every defect above passed a fully green suite. The intent vocabulary is generated from the shared schema, so a renamed literal breaks the build rather than silently degrading every request to `default`.

Guards were mutation-checked: the fix reverted, the test confirmed failing, the fix restored.

title: fix: stop the resume header rendering twice and repair pre-v0.134.0 link mojibake
body:
Two unrelated defects that showed up in one screenshot of the résumé preview.

## 1. The header rendered twice

The styled header showed the name and contact line, and then immediately a body section headed with the same name in ALL-CAPS, carrying the title and a second contact line.

Two independent causes, either of which reproduces it alone:

**Rust** — `parse_line` decided "this line is the candidate's name" from the raw line index. PDF extraction routinely emits a leading blank line, so the real name landed at index 1, missed the rule, matched `is_all_caps_section_heading` instead, and became a section header. That flips `seen_section` immediately, so the title and contact lines below were swallowed into a section named after the candidate while `header.name`/`header.contact` stayed empty and `apply_to_header` refilled them from the contact profile. The rule now keys on the first line **with content**; `idx == 0` is kept as its own arm so the original behaviour cannot regress.

**TypeScript** — `seedHeaderFromProfile` only recognised the document's own name line at exactly index 0. An ALL-CAPS name passes `isAllCapsSectionHeading`, so it read as a section boundary and the profile's name was inserted *above* it; a leading blank line produced the same shape one index down. The contact scan then broke on that line and spliced a second contact line in too. It now searches the header block for the line that already *is* the profile's name and overwrites that one in place.

Review caught three further defects in that change:
- `nameKey` claimed NFKD folds accented variants together. It does not — NFKD splits a composed character into base + combining mark, the mark is category `Mn`, and the `[^\p{L}\p{N}]+` collapse turned it into a **space**. `François` became `franc ois` and stopped matching `FRANCOIS`, so the fix silently didn't fire for accented names.
- An ALL-CAPS `fullName` in the profile left the reconciled line ALL-CAPS, so the contact scan re-tripped on it and produced a fresh duplicate.
- With no blank line anywhere in the document, the search could reconcile an occurrence of the name in the *body* and leave the header with no name at all.

## 2. Project links arrived as mojibake

A PDF text string (PDF 32000-1 §7.9.2.2) is UTF-16BE behind a `FE FF` BOM or PDFDocEncoded, never UTF-8. #955 added `pdf_text_string` to decode it, but could not touch text already written — so stored anchors still read as two replacement chars followed by every character interleaved with its NUL high byte, matched no project title, and left every link heaped at the end of the section.

`repair_utf16_mojibake` reverses it, anchored on the corruption's own shape: it requires the BOM marker followed by a NUL, then consumes only the `(NUL, ASCII)` pairs it can reconstruct. Two appended migrations rewrite the affected rows in `documents` and `ai_generations`, and the insert/update/import paths repair on write so restoring a pre-fix backup cannot re-inject the corruption.

Review shaped this one substantially:
- A per-row `UPDATE` error was swallowed. That does not do what it looks like: on `SQLITE_FULL`/`IOERR`/`BUSY` SQLite auto-rolls-back the enclosing transaction, so the loop continues in autocommit and the following `PRAGMA user_version` commits on its own — durably marking the migration applied with the row never repaired and never retried. Demonstrated by injecting `SQLITE_FULL` on a real WAL database. Store opens are already non-fatal in `lib.rs`, so propagating costs a session, not the app.
- The strip was document-wide, which deleted legitimate adjacent replacement characters elsewhere in a résumé and fused words on the html/rtf import paths.
- A UTF-16 anchor with non-ASCII code units became plausible garbage with its markers erased, destroying both the byte pairing that still made it recoverable and the marker a later repair would search for. Those rows are now left alone.
- The repair rewrote `documents.text` but left `keywords_json`, `indexed` and the `vectors` row pinned to the corrupt text, so the ATS score beside the corrected résumé would have stayed computed from mojibake forever. It now clears them.
- Both migrations snapshot the affected rows before rewriting.

## 3. Docs

`apps/landing` has been a real workspace for a while and appeared in none of the four Markdown directory listings. `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` was the stalest: it called the desktop app `apps/tauri`, pointed at a `src/tauri-client.ts` that is a directory, and also omitted `apps/extension` and `packages/translations`. ADR-0021 is corrected for the in-place name reconciliation.

## Verification

`pnpm test` 4945 pass · `pnpm typecheck` clean · `pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0` clean · `pnpm check:agent-system` in sync · `cargo test --all-features` 3208 pass · `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -D warnings` clean · `cargo test --test architecture` 18/18.

Every new guard was mutation-checked: the fix reverted, the test confirmed failing, the fix restored.

## Not included

The generation failure at reasoning effort `high` (repeating thinking text, flow resetting to the wizard) is diagnosed but deliberately left out — it is a separate concern and lands as a follow-up.

title: ui: explain what the job match and trust badges mean on hover
body:
Both job badges showed a verdict with no way to learn what it meant.

- **`MatchBand`** rendered the bare word `High` with **no description at all** on the Autopilot card. The jobs list did have a popover, but its copy is a disclaimer (*"not the employer's decision"*) that never said what the tier itself means.
- **`TrustBadge`** listed *which checks failed* (`"Suspicious domain"`) but never the verdict — which is the part that tells a reader whether to skip a posting or just look twice.

Now: `MatchBand` carries a plain-language description, and `TrustBadge` leads its tooltip with the level's meaning before the failed-check list.

## Why `title` and not a popover

`TrustBadge` uses a `HoverPopover`, so that was the obvious thing to reach for. It doesn't work for `MatchBand`:

- The Autopilot card renders the band **inside a `<Button>`** — a focusable trigger there is invalid button-in-button HTML.
- `PostingListItem` rows are an **aria-activedescendant listbox** — a trigger would add a tab stop per row.

Both constraints are already documented in comments at those call sites (`TrustBadge` passes `interactive={false}` for the same reasons). A native `title` is hover-capable and focusable-free, so it is safe in both, and it pairs with an sr-only suffix for screen readers.

`RowMatchScore` already owns a real popover, so it opts out with `describe={false}` and folds the tier sentence into its own copy — otherwise a browser tooltip would fire alongside it saying a shorter version of the same thing.

## Per-variant, not just per-tier

A `coverage` High is keyword overlap with **no AI scoring behind it**; a `combined` High blends meaning and keywords. One shared sentence would have to be vague enough to be true of both, which is how a tooltip stops being worth reading. A test asserts the two variants don't say the same thing.

## One latent bug

`TrustBadge`'s detail block was gated on the flag list being non-empty, so a flagged-but-reasonless assessment rendered a bare badge with nothing to explain it. Now gated on `interactive` alone — the level description always exists.

## Testing note

`match-band.test.tsx` stubs `t` to echo raw keys, so it **structurally cannot** catch a missing translation, and the key is built at runtime from tier + variant (`jobs.matchBand.desc.<variant>.<tier>`) so TypeScript can't either. Added `match-band.i18n.test.tsx` using real translations — the same rationale `trust-badge.test.tsx` already documents in its header — and extended the trust-badge suite.

I deleted two keys to check these guards aren't theater: **4 tests went red.** Restored after.

| `pnpm --filter @ajh/desktop test` | 259 files / 2960 pass (14 new) |

**Not verified:** not looked at running. The `title` tooltip is the browser's own, so it has a ~1s delay and no styling — on the Autopilot card that's the only option without restructuring the row out of its `<Button>`. If the delay feels wrong there, that restructure is the follow-up.

Three related changes to the résumé/model surfaces, folded into one PR.

## 1 · `fix:` pdf link anchors arrived as mojibake

**Reported symptom:** generated résumés showed a block of links like
`[��g�i�t�h�u�b�.�c�o�m/…](https://github.com/…)`, detached from their project
titles.

A PDF *text string* (PDF 32000-1 §7.9.2.2) is not UTF-8 — it is either
PDFDocEncoded or UTF-16BE behind a `FE FF` BOM, and Typst, LaTeX and Word all
emit the UTF-16BE form for annotation `/Contents`. `extraction/pdf.rs` read it
with `from_utf8_lossy`, producing the BOM as `��` followed by every ASCII
character interleaved with its NUL high byte.

Both reported symptoms are one bug. The extractor writes those anchors into the
`\n---\n` reference block; `packages/prompts/src/generate/links` matches anchor →
project title to place each link. A mojibake anchor matches nothing, so every
link fell through to the unmatched-links path (`links.ts:1112`) and was spliced
in as its own item.

Adds `pdf_text_string()` (UTF-16BE / UTF-16LE / UTF-8-with-BOM / passthrough),
applied at all three sites sharing the shape: the `/Contents` anchor, the `/URI`,
and `validate/mod.rs`'s round-trip URL check.

⚠️ **Requires re-importing the résumé PDF** — the fix is at extraction time, so
already-extracted text stays mangled. I have not verified the placement fix
end-to-end on a real PDF; if links still land in a block after a fresh import,
that is a separate bug in the anchor→title matcher.

## 2 · `feat:` trim panel — rank the weakest lines for this posting

When the rendered preview exceeds the export market's customary length, an
advisory panel ranks the résumé's bullets by how little of *this* posting's
vocabulary each carries, weakest first, ties longest-first.

Embedding-free by design: reuses the `documents/keywords` kernel and the same
JD-derived stemmer as `score_one`, so the panel can never disagree with the match
score for the same pair. Zero model calls, works offline. Per-line embeddings
would have meant ~40 calls per résumé/job pair plus a cache table, and would
break whenever Ollama is down.

**Read-only** — it never edits the document; the user cuts in the editor beside it.

Adds `LocaleProfile::max_pages`, the market's customary page *count* — distinct
from `page_size`, the physical sheet on the same struct. These are hiring
conventions with no published standard (anglophone + FR/NL 2, DACH + generic-EU
3), documented as such on the field.

## 3 · `ui:` effort picker wherever a model is selected

The reasoning-effort picker only appeared in the three Settings provider
sections. `ModelSelector` is the one shared component behind all ~14 model-picking
surfaces and already computes the provider/model/baseUrl the picker needs, so
this is a single insertion there — AI Generate, Analyze, Tailor, Autopilot,
resume builder, GitHub import, interview prep, apply-by-email, referral modal and
onboarding all pick it up with no call-site changes.

Safe to render unconditionally: `EffortPicker` already returns `null` unless the
backend reports `effortLevels` for the selected model.

Moved `EffortPicker` from `features/settings/` to `components/ui/` — a shared
component importing from a feature is the wrong direction under rule 9. Added a
`compact` variant that drops the uppercase section heading (which would read as a
settings section leaking into a panel) while keeping an `aria-label` and a leading
icon.

The stored value stays **per-provider** — changing it from any surface changes it
for that provider everywhere, the same preference Settings writes.

title: fix: upload only our own debug files to sentry
body:
Found by inspecting the first real release run ([30741386889](https://github.com/saeedkolivand/ai-job-hunter-app/actions/runs/30741386889)).

## The good news first

Everything from #927/#929 worked on all four matrix legs: symbol upload `success`, flag step correctly `skipped`, assets published before symbols, no cascade into the updater jobs, `Created release 0.132.0`. **The auth token is valid** — that was the one thing tests could not prove.

## The bug

```
> Uploaded 474 missing debug information files
```

Per leg. ~1900 per release. What actually went up:

```
release/build/aws-lc-sys-.../out/chacha20_poly1305_x86_64.o
release/build/proc-macro2-.../build-script-build
release/deps/libscroll_derive-....so
AI Job Hunter.AppDir/usr/lib/libicudata.so.70
AI Job Hunter.AppDir/usr/lib/libudev.so.1
AI Job Hunter.AppDir/usr/bin/ajh-tauri          ← the only one that matters
```

Dependency build scripts, proc-macro `.so`s, `ring`/`aws-lc-sys` object files, and the third-party system libraries bundled into the AppImage. I had pointed `sentry-cli debug-files upload` at the whole `target/` tree.

## The fix, and why it is derived rather than guessed

Scoped to `ajh_tauri*` under `release/deps`. I took the paths **from that run's logs instead of inferring them**, which turned out to matter — my first attempt at this patch guessed `target/<triple>/release/ajh-tauri.dSYM` and would have been wrong on two platforms:

| Platform | Actual |
| --- | --- |
| Linux | `release/deps/ajh_tauri-<hash>` |
| Windows | `release\deps\ajh_tauri.exe` + **`ajh_tauri.pdb`** |
| macOS | `<triple>/release/deps/ajh_tauri-<hash>` + `.dSYM` |

On every platform the artifacts carry the **library** name (`ajh_tauri`, underscore) and sit in `deps/` — not the bin name at `release/ajh-tauri`. The guessed path would have uploaded the macOS binary **with no debug companion**: symbolication silently degraded, which is this feature's signature failure.

The copies under `release/`, `bundle/appimage/` and `bundle/deb/` are hardlinks that dedupe to the same debug id, so nothing is lost by ignoring them.

Also guarded the per-triple directory behind a non-empty check — with `matrix.target` empty the path collapses to `target//release/deps`, the same directory, enumerating everything twice.

## Verification

Simulated all three real layouts plus the empty case:

```
linux   -> 2: deps/ajh_tauri-fa4fa53a  deps/ajh_tauri-fa4fa53a.d
windows -> 2: deps/ajh_tauri.exe       deps/ajh_tauri.pdb
macos   -> 2: <triple>/deps/ajh_tauri-d8c3e74  <triple>/deps/ajh_tauri-d8c3e74.dSYM
empty   -> 0  (fails loudly, per the existing guard)
```

474 → 2 per leg, debug companion included in every case. YAML parses, step body passes `bash -n`, `continue-on-error` untouched (see ADR-0020 for why it must stay).

title: fix: keep project links out of the resume header and make them work
body:
Fixes three defects reported from one generated résumé.

## Project URLs rendered on the contact line

Project sites were swept into the contact profile's extra links at import, so the exported header rendered them on the contact line **and** again in PROJECTS. Only platform profiles may seed extra links now, and website selection prefers an apex over its own subdomains, so it no longer depends on the order links happen to appear in the source PDF.

## PROJECTS read as `Name — same-name-slug`, with no links

The prompt asked for that shape, and link injection matched the machine label literally while the PDF extractor humanised it differently — so the label never matched and nothing linked. Items now carry their real name; matching is normalised and assigns each link to its best line; job-board and non-personal profile URLs are dropped rather than becoming invented projects; and a link that still matches nothing is placed in the localized projects section or left unplaced, never appended as an orphan.

## The header in the editor differed from the exported one

Edits to it were silently discarded from PDF and DOCX while still shipping in TXT and clipboard copy. The document text now owns the header at export; the profile seeds it at generation and fills only what the text leaves blank. See [ADR-0021](docs/adr/0021-editor-owns-resume-header.md).

## Review notes

This went through three security rounds and a three-pass review ensemble before opening. Findings worth calling out, because each was invisible in the diff and only appeared when a reviewer executed the code:

- The header-seeding scan could **delete résumé content** — an entire job, a skills line, a project link — for four of the seven locales the app generates for, and for English résumés whose first heading wasn't in the recognised list. Seeding now only ever replaces one line or inserts; removal is structurally impossible.
- The Resume Builder path was never seeded, so making export fallback-only would have shipped the model's invented contact line. Both generation paths now seed through one helper, and the prompt's false promise that the line "will be replaced on export" is gone.
- A profile with only a name never seeded it, and export could not rescue it.
- The two profile lookups were unguarded and could discard a completed, already-paid-for generation.

Rules that exist in both Rust and TypeScript are now gated by shared JSON fixtures asserted from both sides, and the section-name list is read from its fixture by TypeScript rather than duplicated — after three separate bugs this session traced to a mirrored rule whose comment claimed a parity it did not have.

title: fix: warn when local ollama has no account key for company research
body:
Company research on local Ollama needs a free Ollama **account key** (credential slot `ollama-cloud`), because Ollama has no model-side web search — the app calls its web search API instead. Without the key the backend returns nothing and the renderer swallows the failure, so a missing key looked exactly like *"found nothing"*, and the cover letter was generated ungrounded with no signal to the user.

## What changed

The interview-questions modal already warned about this, and the AI-Generate fine-tune step carried its own guarded copy of the same rule. Both now consume one shared hook, and the hint appears beside the "research company" toggle in the tailor flow too. No new strings — the existing translation is reused.

## Review notes

The pre-PR review caught that the repo had **two** implementations of this predicate, and the first attempt at consolidation extracted the wrong one — dropping a cold-boot guard added by #682. Both defaults fail *into* the hint (`activeProvider` defaults to `ollama` before the config resolves, `has` defaults to `false` before the key query resolves), so an unguarded check tells a user who **already has** the key that they need to add it, on first paint of a cold session. Reproduced by executing the hook against a stub client.

The shared hook now guards both pending windows — including the key-query one, which the fine-tune copy never covered — and the fine-tune step was migrated, so there is genuinely one predicate in one place rather than two.

The hint is announced (`role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`): the provider picker sits directly above it, so switching providers makes it appear in response to the user's own action, and `TailorWizard` has no ambient live region the way its sibling wizards do.

Tests were tightened alongside: the a11y attributes are now asserted by role rather than text (stripping them fails the suite), and the credential-slot argument is asserted rather than discarded by the mock — previously, changing `ollama-cloud` to `ollama` would have kept every test green while pinning the hint on for every Ollama user in production.
